tagline: Lightweight Python toolkit for neutralizing gendered language in AI text.
short_description: A dependency-free Python library that debiases and rebias gendered terms in text labels using fast heuristics, for cleaning training data and filtering model outputs.
long_description: nexttext is a lightweight Python toolkit for neutralizing and re-framing text to reduce noise, hidden skew, and unwanted artifacts in AI pipelines. It works on both human-annotated input labels and model-generated labels, using simple, fast heuristics to neutralise gendered or stereotypical language (debias) and optionally reintroduce controlled skew for testing and validation (rebias), including a context-aware strategy. It ships with no heavy dependencies, requires Python 3.9+, and is released under the MIT license, targeting tasks like training data cleanup, inference filtering, and standardization of labels across datasets.
notes: Published to GitHub Pages at https://jpeckenpaugh.github.io/nexttext/ (HTTP 200); previously repo-only. Also a reusable pip-installable library (pyproject name=nexttext, v0.1.0) with MIT license.
